reconcile.note: Clarke distinguishes the diffused day-one light from the sun and stars later constituted as its light-bearers on day four.

discrepancy.note: Paine objects that Genesis places three days and nights, with evenings and mornings, before any sun exists to cause them.

quotes.text: They make there to have been three days and three nights, evenings and mornings, before there was a sun; when it is the presence or absence of the sun that is the cause of day and night, and what is called his rising and setting that of morning and evening.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II

sides.snippet: God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. There was evening and there was morning, one day.
sides.verseText: God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. There was evening and there was morning, one day.

sides.snippet: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.
